The relatively modest length of the pups reflects the energetic constraints of a viviparous reproductive mode in which yolk-dependent embryos develop without a placental connection. Within the broader Squalus genus, this birth length is intermediate, similar to that recorded in Squalus acutipennis but smaller than in the larger-bodied Squalus acanthias.
